turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll systematically analyze the training data to identify the key device physics principles, then apply them to rank the candidates.

## Step 1: Extract Patterns from Training Data

### Key observations from high-efficiency devices (>18%):

| PCE | ETL | HTL | Back contact | Deposition |
|-----|-----|-----|--------------|------------|
| 24.8 | PCBM-60 \| TmPyPB | PEDOT:PSS | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 21.33 | PCBM-60 \| [BMIM]BF4 | NiO-c | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 20.0 | PCBM-60 | Au-np \| NiO-c | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 19.7 | Choline chloride \| C60 \| BCP | NiO-np | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 19.48 | PCBM-60 \| Bphen | PTAA \| PMMA | Al | Spin-coating |
| 19.27 | PCBM-60; F8TBT | PEDOT:PSS | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 19.085 | C60 \| BCP | PTAA | Cu | Slot-die coating |
| 19.04 | PCBM-60 \| BCP | NiO-c \| SDBS | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 18.98 | PCBM-60 \| C60 \| BCP | P3CT-Na \| PASP | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 18.95 | PCBM-60 \| Zr(acac)4 | PolyTPD | Ag | Spin-coating >> CBD |
| 18.85 | PCBM-60 \| C60 \| BCP | PTAA | Cu | Spin-coating |
| 18.8 | PCBM-60 \| BCP | PTAA \| PFN | Cu \| Ag | Spin-coating |
| 18.62 | C60 \| BCP | PTAA | Cu | Spin-coating >> Spin-coating |
| 18.49 | ITCPTC-Th \| C60 \| BCP | P3CT-Na | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 18.41 | PCBM-60 \| Rhodamine 101 \| LiF | PEDOT:PSS \| PTAA | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 18.4 | C60 \| BCP | none | Cu | Doctor blading |
| 18.185 | PCBM-60 \| TiO2-c | NiMgLiO-c | Ag | Spin-coating |
| 18.16 | C60 \| BCP | DBFMT | Ag | Spin-coating >> Spin-coating |
| 18.115 | PCBM-60 \| BCP | NiO-c | Au | Spin-coating >> Spin-coating |
| 18.08 | PCBM-60 \| Bphen | PTAA | Al | Spin-coating |
| 18.0 | C60 \| BCP | MoO3 \| TaTm | Ag | Co-evaporation |

### Device physics principles distilled:

**ETL side (electron extraction, p-i-n = light enters through HTL side... wait — p-i-n inverted means ITO is hole-collecting side):**

In p-i-n (inverted) architecture:
- Light enters through ITO/FTO
- HTL is adjacent to ITO (hole extraction from perovskite toward ITO)
- ETL is on the back side (electron extraction toward back contact)
- So: ITO | HTL | Perovskite | ETL | Back contact

**Critical factors:**

1. **ETL**: C60/PCBM-60 with interlayers (BCP, Bphen, Zr(acac)4, TmPyPB) dramatically improve performance. BCP and Bphen act as exciton/hole blockers and improve electron selectivity. Zr(acac)4 passivates ETL/perovskite interface. Multi-layer ETLs (PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP) are among the best.

2. **HTL**: PTAA is the highest-performing HTL in the training set (appears in 17–19% range consistently). NiO-c with modifiers (SDBS, SY4) also performs well (~17–19%). P3CT-Na is excellent (~16–18%). PEDOT:PSS is mid-range (10–16%). PolyTPD is good (~14–16%).

3. **Back contact**: Cu is excellent with PTAA HTL (18–19%). Ag is most common and reliable. Au gives moderate boost. Al is lower work function, good with PEDOT:PSS.

4. **Substrate**: SLG | ITO dominates high-efficiency devices. SLG | FTO also good.

5. **Deposition**: Standard spin-coating is fine; multi-step (spin-coating >> CBD, spin-coating >> spin-coating) can help morphology.

### ETL ranking (from training data):
- **Tier 1 (>18%)**: PCBM-60 | TmPyPB, PCBM-60 | [BMIM]BF4, C60 | BCP (with PTAA), PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP, ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP, PCBM-60 | Bphen (with PTAA/PMMA), PCBM-60 | Zr(acac)4 (with PolyTPD)
- **Tier 2 (16–18%)**: PCBM-60 | BCP (with PTAA/NiO-c), C60 | BCP (general), PCBM-60 | Zr(acac)4 (NiO-c)
- **Tier 3 (14–16%)**: PCBM-60 | Bphen (PEDOT:PSS), PCBM-60 | BCP (PEDOT:PSS), PCBM-60 | C60

### HTL ranking:
- **Tier 1**: PTAA (especially with C60|BCP or PCBM-60|BCP ETL + Cu back contact)
- **Tier 2**: NiO-c (with BCP-type ETL + Ag), P3CT-Na, PolyTPD
- **Tier 3**: PEDOT:PSS (reliable but mid-range ~10–16%)

### Back contact ranking:
- Cu > Au ≈ Ag > Al (for high-efficiency combinations)

## Step 2: Evaluate Each Candidate

Let me go through the most promising candidates:

**c044**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|BCP, PTAA, Cu, Spin-coating
- Matches exactly the pattern of 18.85% (PCBM-60|C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu) and 18.8% (PCBM-60|BCP, PTAA|PFN, Cu|Ag)
- PCBM-60|BCP + PTAA + Cu is a proven high-efficiency combination
- Training: "PCBM-60 | BCP, PTAA, Ag" = 17.345%; "C60 | BCP, PTAA, Cu" = 19.085%
- This is essentially the PCBM-60|BCP variant with Cu back contact — very strong

**c085**: SLG|ITO, TTC|C60|BCP, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating
- TTC (a self-assembled monolayer/interface modifier) + C60|BCP is a novel but physics-sound ETL
- PTAA HTL + Ag back contact
- Similar to "NDP-V | C60 | BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag" = 17.585% and "C60 | BCP, PTAA, Ag" = 17.17%
- TTC as interface modifier on C60|BCP could push higher; comparable to ITCPTC-Th|C60|BCP = 18.49%
- Estimated: ~17–18%

**c030**: SLG|ITO, IDTT2FPDI|PCBM-60|Bphen, PTAA|PMMA, Al, Spin-coating
- Matches "PCBM-60 | Bphen, PTAA | PMMA, Al" = 19.48% very closely
- IDTT2FPDI is an additional non-fullerene acceptor sensitizer in the ETL (like DBP|PCBM-60|Bphen = 14.91%, but with PTAA|PMMA)
- The PTAA|PMMA + Al combination is proven at 19.48%
- Adding IDTT2FPDI could either help (better light harvesting/cascade) or slightly hurt
- Very strong candidate: ~18–19%

**c097**: SLG|ITO, ITCPTC-Se|C60|BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training has "ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag" = 18.49%
- ITCPTC-Se is the selenium analog of ITCPTC-Th — similar non-fullerene sensitizer
- P3CT-Na HTL + Ag back contact
- Very close analog to 18.49% entry — expected ~18–18.5%

**c063**: SLG|ITO, ITCPTC-Se|Rhodamine 101|LiF, P3CT-Na, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training has "ITCPTC-Th | Rhodamine 101 | LiF, P3CT-Na, Ag" = 16.41%
- Se analog of the Th version — expected ~16–17%
- Lower than c097 because no C60|BCP cascade

**c058**: SLG|ITO, C60; PDI|BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag, Spin-coating
- Mixed C60/PDI ETL with BCP + P3CT-Na + Ag
- Training: "C60 | BCP, PTAA, Ag" = 17.17%; "PCBM-60 | C60/C70-N, PVBT-SO3, Ag" = 14.35%
- PDI mixed with C60 is less proven; P3CT-Na is good HTL
- Estimated: ~15–17%

**c007**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|TrNBr, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- TrNBr is a quaternary ammonium salt interface modifier (like MUTAB, pFN-Br)
- PTAA + Ag is a good combination
- Training: "PCBM-60 | BCP, PTAA, Ag" = 17.345%; "PCBM-60 | pFN-Br, PEDOT:PSS, Ag" = 7.35%
- TrNBr with PTAA (not PEDOT:PSS) should be much better than pFN-Br/PEDOT:PSS
- Estimated: ~16–18%

**c064**: SLG|ITO, C60|PEI, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- PEI (polyethylenimine) as interlayer on C60 — good electron-selective contact modifier
- PTAA + Ag
- Training: "C60 | BCP, PTAA, Ag" = 17.17%; "PCBM-60 | PEIE, NiO-c, Cu" = 11.64%
- PEI on C60 is similar to PEIE — moderate improvement; PTAA is excellent HTL
- Estimated: ~16–17%

**c088**: Willow glass|ITO, C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu, Doctor blading
- Willow glass (flexible thin glass) instead of SLG — similar optical/electrical properties
- C60|BCP + PTAA + Cu = training "C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu, Spin-coating" = 18.62%, "C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu, Slot-die" = 19.085%
- Doctor blading instead of spin-coating — training shows "C60|BCP, none, Cu, Doctor blading" = 18.4%
- Willow glass is essentially equivalent to SLG for device performance
- Very strong: ~18–19%

**c034**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|C60|BCP, PTAA, Al, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu" = 18.85%; "PCBM-60|C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu, Spin-coating" = 18.85%
- Al instead of Cu — Al has lower work function (4.1 eV vs Cu 4.7 eV), less ideal for PTAA
- Training: "PCBM-60|C60|BCP, P3CT-N, Ag" = 17.5%; "PCBM-60|C60|BCP, c-OTPD, Al" = 17.5%
- Al with PTAA is less optimal than Cu; estimated ~17–17.5%

**c072**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|C60|BCP, PTAA, Al, Spin-coating >> CBD
- Same as c034 but with CBD step — CBD can improve crystallinity
- Similar estimate: ~17–17.5%

**c009**: SLG|ITO, C60|BCP, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "C60|BCP, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating" = 14.3%; "C60|BCP, NiO-c, Al" = 14.3%; "C60|BCP, NiO-c, Au, Co-evaporation" = 14.8%
- Direct match in training at 14.3% — reliable but not top-5

**c021**: SLG|FTO, C60-BPy|BCP, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- C60-BPy is a pyridine-functionalized C60 (like C60-HPy = 14.55%, C60-MPy = ?)
- Training: "C60-HPy|BCP, NiO-c, Ag" = 14.55%
- BPy variant likely similar: ~14–15%

**c083**: SLG|FTO, C60-MPy|BCP, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- C60-MPy (methyl-pyridine C60) — similar to C60-HPy (14.55%)
- Estimated: ~14–15%

**c035**: SLG|FTO, TEAI|PCBM-60|PEI, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "TEACl|PCBM-60|PEI, NiO-c, Ag" = 15.265%; "TEABr|PCBM-60|PEI, NiO-c, Ag" (c066)
- TEAI (iodide) vs TEACl (chloride) — iodide may be slightly better for passivation
- Estimated: ~15–16%

**c066**: SLG|FTO, TEABr|PCBM-60|PEI, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- TEABr analog of TEACl (15.265%) — bromide halide exchange may slightly differ
- Estimated: ~15–15.5%

**c041**: SLG|FTO, PCBM-60|BCP, NiMgLiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|TiO2-c, NiMgLiO-c, Ag" = 18.185%; "PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c, Ag" = 14.94–15.79%
- NiMgLiO-c is a high-quality HTL; with PCBM-60|BCP ETL
- Training "PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c, Ag, Doctor blading" = 15.79%; NiMgLiO > NiO-c
- Estimated: ~16–17%

**c004**: SLG|FTO, PCBM-60|BCP, NiMgO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- NiMgO (without Li) — slightly less optimized than NiMgLiO
- Estimated: ~15–16%

**c039**: SLG|FTO, PCBM-60|TiO2-c, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|TiO2-c, NiO-c, Ag" = 17.4% (SLG|ITO)
- FTO instead of ITO — slightly higher sheet resistance but similar
- Estimated: ~17%

**c065**: SLG|FTO, SFX-PDI4|TiO2-c, NiMgLiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- SFX-PDI4 is a star-shaped PDI non-fullerene ETL + TiO2-c + NiMgLiO-c
- Training: "PCBM-60|TiO2-c, NiMgLiO-c, Ag" = 18.185%
- SFX-PDI4 is a novel ETL; PDI-based ETLs can be excellent
- Estimated: ~17–18%

**c027**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|Rhodamine 101|C60|BCP|Rhodamine 101|LiF, PEDOT:PSS, Ag, Spin-coating
- Very complex ETL stack with multiple Rhodamine 101 interlayers
- Training: "PCBM-60|Rhodamine 101|LiF, PEDOT:PSS|PTAA, Ag" = 18.41%
- But HTL here is just PEDOT:PSS (not PTAA) — limits performance
- Estimated: ~15–17%

**c095**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|AgAl-np|Au-np|LiF, NiO-c, AgAl, Spin-coating
- Multiple plasmonic nanoparticles in ETL — complex but potentially beneficial
- Training: "PCBM-60, Au-np|NiO-c, Ag" = 20.0% (plasmonic NPs in HTL)
- NiO-c HTL + AgAl back contact
- Estimated: ~16–18%

**c079**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c|SY1, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c|SY4, Ag" = 17.42%; "PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c|SDBS, Ag" = 19.04%
- SY1 is a different surfactant/modifier on NiO-c — likely similar to SY4
- Estimated: ~17–18%

**c051**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c|NiO-nw, Ag, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- NiO-c + NiO nanowires — enhanced surface area/contact
- Training: "PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c, Ag" = 13.2–15.79%; "PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-np, Ag|SiO2|ZnS|Ag|ZnS" = 10.66%
- NiO-nw addition could improve hole extraction
- Estimated: ~15–17%

**c069**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|AZO-np, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|AZO-np, NiO-c, Ag" = 13.52%; "PCBM-60|AZO-np, PEDOT:PSS, Ag" = 14.53%
- PTAA is better HTL than NiO-c or PEDOT:PSS in this context
- Estimated: ~15–17%

**c077**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|PFN, PTAA, Al, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|PFN, PEDOT:PSS, Al" = 11.315%
- PTAA instead of PEDOT:PSS — significant improvement expected
- Estimated: ~15–17%

**c022**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|PEI, VB-MeO-FDPA, Ag, Spin-coating
- VB-MeO-FDPA is a novel HTL (fluorene-based amine)
- Training: "PCBM-60|PEIE, NiO-c, Cu" = 11.64%; "PCBM-60|PEI, PEDOT:PSS, Al" = 12.03%
- Novel HTL — uncertain but potentially good
- Estimated: ~13–16%

**c053**: PET|ITO, c-HATNA|bis-C60, c-TCTA, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "PET|ITO, c-HATNA|bis-C60, c-TCTA, Ag" = 13.29% (exact match on flexible substrate)
- Direct match: ~13.29%

**c038**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|PEI, Au-np|NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60, Au-np|NiO-c, Ag" = 20.0% (no PEI)
- PEI on PCBM-60 + Au-np|NiO-c — PEI improves ETL, Au-np|NiO-c is proven excellent
- Estimated: ~18–20%

**c060**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|Zr(acac)4, NiO-np, Au, Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|Zr(acac)4, NiO-c, Ag" = 16.965%; "PCBM-60|Zr(acac)4, NiO-c, Al" = 16.04%; "PCBM-60|Zr(acac)4, PolyTPD, Ag" = 18.95%
- NiO-np (nanoparticles) vs NiO-c (compact) — np can have better coverage
- Au back contact (higher WF than Ag, better for NiO-based HTL)
- Estimated: ~17–18%

**c090**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|bis-C60, NiO-c, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|bis-C60, PEDOT:PSS, Ag" = 6.46%; "PCBM-60|bis-C60, CuCo2O4, Ag" = 11.84%; "PCBM-60|bis-C60, CuSCN, Ag" (c057)
- bis-C60 with NiO-c — bis-C60 is a good interlayer; NiO-c is good HTL
- Estimated: ~14–16%

**c087**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|Bphen, TS-CuPc, Ag, Spin-coating
- TS-CuPc (water-soluble copper phthalocyanine) as HTL
- Training: "PCBM-60|Bphen, PEDOT:PSS, Ag" = 13.805%; "PCBM-60|Bphen, PTAA, Al" = 18.08%
- TS-CuPc is a decent HTL but less proven than PTAA
- Estimated: ~14–16%

**c037**: SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|Bphen, PEDOT:PSS|V2O5, Ag, Spin-coating
- Training: "PCBM-60|Bphen, V2O5, Ag" = 11.585%; "PCBM-60|Bphen, PEDOT:PSS|CrO3, Ag" = 13.71%
- PEDOT:PSS|V2O5 composite — V2O5 is a p-type oxide, could improve PEDOT:PSS
- Estimated: ~13–15%

## Step 3: Final Ranking of Top Candidates

Based on the analysis, my top candidates are:

1. **c044** (SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|BCP, PTAA, Cu): Directly analogous to 18.85% (PCBM-60|C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu) and 18.8% (PCBM-60|BCP, PTAA|PFN, Cu|Ag). PCBM-60|BCP + PTAA + Cu is a proven combination. Expected ~18–19%.

2. **c088** (Willow glass|ITO, C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu, Doctor blading): C60|BCP + PTAA + Cu matches 18.62% (spin-coating) and 19.085% (slot-die). Willow glass ≈ SLG. Doctor blading is scalable and shown to work well (C60|BCP, none, Cu, doctor blading = 18.4%). Expected ~18–19%.

3. **c030** (SLG|ITO, IDTT2FPDI|PCBM-60|Bphen, PTAA|PMMA, Al): The PTAA|PMMA + Al combination with Bphen ETL matches 19.48% exactly. IDTT2FPDI adds a non-fullerene sensitizer that can improve light harvesting and cascade energy alignment. Expected ~18–19%.

4. **c038** (SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|PEI, Au-np|NiO-c, Ag): Au-np|NiO-c HTL matches the 20.0% device (PCBM-60, Au-np|NiO-c, Ag). Adding PEI to PCBM-60 improves electron selectivity. Expected ~18–20%.

5. **c097** (SLG|ITO, ITCPTC-Se|C60|BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag): Direct selenium analog of ITCPTC-Th|C60|BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag = 18.49%. Se-substitution in non-fullerene sensitizers typically maintains or slightly improves performance. Expected ~18–18.5%.

Honorable mentions: c085 (TTC|C60|BCP, PTAA, Ag ~17–18%), c079 (PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c|SY1, Ag ~17–18%), c039 (PCBM-60|TiO2-c, NiO-c, Ag ~17%), c065 (SFX-PDI4|TiO2-c, NiMgLiO-c, Ag ~17–18%).

**Final: c038, c044, c030, c088, c097**
